title: Cross-region runway & token-econ playbook
body:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook for estimating multi-region GPU-hour runway and per-1M-token unit economics. This is intentionally informal — contains rough formulas, scenario buckets, and open questions to drive the next modeling sprint. Use this when we need a fast sanity check (sales asks, infra exec sync, SRE planning).

High-level goal:
- Produce a micro-decision framework: given committed GPU-hours and a region mix, estimate how many 1M-token units we can serve and the expected $/1M-token across hardware types and model families.
- Surface breakpoints where Dedicated/reserved capacity becomes favorable vs Hosted/spot mix.

Assumptions (base-case):
- Model families and representative throughput and memory footprint (inference-mode, KV-cache-friendly):
  * small-quant (4-bit quant) 7B -> 25 tokens/sec on A100, 40 tok/s on H100, 65 tok/s on L4 (batching dependent)
  * medium 13B -> 12 tok/s on A100, 20 tok/s on H100, 35 tok/s on L4
  * large 70B (q8) -> 3 tok/s on A100, 5 tok/s on H100, 9 tok/s on L4
- Typical request mix: 60% small, 30% medium, 10% large by token volume. Average tokens per request = 120.
- GPU-hour price (effective after cloud discount + infra ops): A100 = $3.6/hr, H100 = $6.0/hr, L4 = $1.4/hr. (These are blended internal accounting numbers; actual encrypted billing sits elsewhere.)
- Overhead factors: baseline kernel inefficiency / idle = 1.18 (i.e. 18% wasted capacity due to cold starts, imbalanced batching, kv warmup). Spot preemption reserve = 1.07 (to account for capacity safety). Combined safety multiplier = 1.25.

Core formulas (text):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600 * workload_utilization_factor / safety_multiplier
  * workload_utilization_factor approximates active serving time (we use 0.82 as default).
- $ per 1M tokens = gpu_hour_price / (tokens_per_gpu_hour / 1_000_000)

Quick worked example (base-case, L4, small-quant dominant):
- throughput = 65 tok/s -> raw tokens/hour = 65 * 3600 = 234,000
- apply utilization 0.82 -> 191,880 tokens/hr
- apply safety multiplier 1.25 -> effective tokens/hr = 153,504
- per-GPU-hour tokens = 153,504 -> 1M tokens cost = 1_000_000 / 153,504 * $1.4 = $9.12 per 1M tokens

Scenario buckets to include in next sheet run (priority order):
1) Hosted-heavy (80% hosted H100 + 20% L4 spill) — revenue upside, volatile spot exposure.
2) Dedicated-reserved blend (commit on A100 for steady throughput, L4 spot for burst).
3) Low-cost-optimized (L4 primary, aggressive batching, acceptance of slightly higher tail latency).
4) Compliance/Private (on-prem A100/H100 with higher ops overhead: +25% opex).

Regional modifiers (notes for modeling):
- GCP/US-east baseline multiplier = 1.0. EU-west multiplier = 1.15 (higher GPU market cost). APAC regions = 1.25 (higher cloud price + smaller spot pools).
- Latency-driven routing increases cost: if routing forces H100 in APAC for latency, apply +20% on effective price for that traffic slice.

Runway math (how many 3-months of traffic can committed capacity sustain):
- input: committed_gpu_hours_per_month by region, blended model mix by region, forecast growth rate (MoM).
- naive runway months = committed_hours / (projected_gpu_hour_burn_month_one * (1 + growth_rate)^n summed over N months) -> solved for N where capacity >= demand.
- practical rule-of-thumb: for 3x growth in 6 months, we need committed capacity buffer = ~2.2x of month-1 demand to avoid emergency spot buys. (Back-of-envelope; validate with sim.)

Suggested conservative knobs for infra planners (recommendations):
- Keep a dedicated reserve equal to 30% of steady-state committed hours in each critical region (us-east, eu-west). This reduces emergency network egress/latency fallback.
- For performance-sensitive customers, reserve a small H100 slab and route high-qos requests there; use L4 for best-effort / background requests to save cost.
- Implement per-route cost allocation: store approximate $/1M-token per region+model in metadata to enable product billing decisions and customer-facing cost-estimates.

Open questions / data we need to finalize models:
- Real measured throughput numbers for L4 on our runtime with current batching heuristics (INF-1234 tracks this): we still rely on lab numbers that differ from production by ~15-30%.
- Tail-latency impact of aggressive batching under mixed-size traffic; need a small A/B test to measure 95/99th latency when switching utilization from 0.82 -> 0.9.
- Precise cloud effective price by region after committed discounts and partner credits (finance has the canonical numbers; tagged Finance/INF-pricing).

Quick checklist for next iteration (owner: Samir, due: 2025-01-17):
- [ ] Pull actual GPU-hour cost ledger per region for last 90 days (linked to finance query).
- [ ] Run throughput sweep (L4, A100, H100) with production runtime and real request trace (Noah).
- [ ] Build a Monte Carlo sim that samples request size distribution and spot-preemption events; output monthly $/1M-token and probability of emergency scaling (Lena).
- [ ] Publish a short README for Sales to use the per-region $/1M estimates in proposals (Priya).

Notes to self / fragments:
- If average request tokens goes up from 120 -> 180, the per-1M-token cost shifts non-linearly because larger requests increase KV-cache effectiveness (good), but reduce batching packing efficiency (bad). Need to quantify.
- Consider a hybrid billing signal: show customers both token-based price and a per-request latency SLA uplift. This can nudge heavy-request apps to choose Dedicated.

Relevant references/links in case we forget where data lives:
- old econ sheets (read-only): /engineering/infrastructure/gpu-hour-token-econ-heatmap-exploration.json (use for historical priors)
- open ticket to add region multipliers to cost API: JIRA INF-1459

Conclusion (short):
This doc is a playbook for converting capacity (GPU-hours) and regional cost differences into a usable $/1M-token estimate and runway math. Next step: convert scenarios above into a parametrized sheet (Monte Carlo backend) and iterate after the throughput sweep.
